summary.intent: Find out why many PRs were failing CI after a break on main, confirm the user's merged fix worked, and get the failing PR branches updated. The user also wanted to know which background agents were still running.
summary.outcome: Fixed main (#429) was merged, and an agent was launched to merge it into PR branches #428, #430 and #431. The assistant then reported agent status: 5 agents running, 3 finished, and the merged PRs listed.

repo: CI has an 'Entire Gates' check that is excluded when scanning PRs for real failures, since it is a gate rather than a test check.
The first-answer latency gate (150 ms) still fails: 400 ms measured with a floor of about 230 ms (PR #408 merged with this known).
A break on main propagates failures to all open PR branches, so fixed main has to be merged into each branch (done via the merge-main-three agent for #428, #430, #431).
workflow: A single bash loop with git fetch --prune, gh run list and gh pr view with --jq gives a quick overview of main's CI state and each PR's mergeStateStatus and failing checks.
ListAgents separates the assistant's own agents from peer sessions; peer sessions (ten, idle or offline) should not be touched.
Earlier Opus slice agents ran 55 to 118 minutes, so a 2-hour mark without a report is the threshold for checking output and stopping a looping agent.
